newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Fipe inflation at 0.75 pct in Oct 16-Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Fipe inflation at 0.75 pct in Oct 16-Nov 15.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) was 0.75 percent in the Oct 16-Nov 15 period, off an edge from 0.78 percent in the prior four-week period, a Fipe official said.
Juarez Rizzieri, the president of Fipe, said the rise in clothing prices was the main factor driving the price index, which measures prices in the Sao Paulo area.
Clothing prices rose 2.30 percent in the period, which also saw a 1.17 percent hike in transport prices and a 0.63 percent rise in food prices.
The period also saw a dip in education costs.
Rizzieri estimated November inflation could be between 0.50 and 0.75 percent.
He released the following breakdown of the weighted Fipe inflation index for the four-week period ended Oct 15:
-Personal expenses: 0.18 pct rise in the period
-Health care: 0.23 pct rise in the period
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures at weekly intervals.
